properties.name: Toba Caldera
properties.description: Lake Toba is the site of a massive supereruption (~74,000 BP) that created a 100 x 30 km caldera depression and reshaped global climate.
properties.evidence_description: Widespread pumiceous ignimbrite sheets and rhyolitic tephra layers deposited across Northern Sumatra during the ~74,000 BP supereruption.
properties.evidence_significance: Thick ignimbrite field deposits provide direct geological evidence supporting explosive Quaternary supereruptions and high-volume pyroclastic transport.
properties.why_it_matters: Toba represents one of Earth's largest Quaternary supereruptions. Studying its ignimbrite deposits helps scientists understand how catastrophic volcanic events impact global climate and human evolutionary history.

properties.name: Sangiran Early Man Site
properties.description: One of the world's most important hominid fossil localities, yielding numerous Homo erectus fossil remains and Pleistocene vertebrate fossils.
properties.fossil_material: Cranial fragments, mandibular fossils, Stegodon remains
properties.evidence_description: Fossilized cranial fragments and jawbones of Homo erectus discovered within stratified fluvial clay and gravel terraces of the Sangiran Dome.
properties.evidence_significance: Stratified hominid skeletal fossils support the interpretation of early Pleistocene hominin dispersal and floodplain habitat occupation in Southeast Asia.
properties.why_it_matters: Sangiran provides a continuous 1.5-million-year sedimentary record containing over half of all known Homo erectus fossils worldwide, essential for understanding early human migration across Southeast Asia.

properties.name: Mount Merapi
properties.description: An active stratovolcano situated on the Sunda Arc subduction zone, famous for dome-collapse pyroclastic density currents (nuées ardentes — fast-moving hot gas and volcanic debris flows).
properties.evidence_description: Andesitic and basaltic-andesite lava dome fragments, pyroclastic density current deposits, and block-and-ash flow fans on the volcano slopes.
properties.evidence_significance: Slope block-and-ash deposits provide physical evidence consistent with recurring explosive dome-collapse volcanism along active subduction arcs.
properties.why_it_matters: Merapi is one of the world's most active subduction volcanoes. Monitoring its dome-collapse pyroclastic flows provides critical scientific insights into volcanic hazard mitigation in densely populated volcanic arc settings.

properties.name: Belitung Granitic Boulders
properties.description: Striking coastal granite tor formations formed by Early Triassic plutonic intrusion (underground magma cooling) followed by deep tropical weathering and coastal erosion.
properties.evidence_description: Early Triassic Tanjung Pandan granitic tor boulders exposed along coastal shorelines, featuring coarse quartz and feldspar mineral grains.
properties.evidence_significance: Exposed plutonic granites provide evidence consistent with Mesozoic magmatic cooling beneath ancient continental Sundaland crust.
properties.why_it_matters: The Tanjung Pandan granites reveal the Mesozoic magmatic assembly of Sundaland. Tropical tor weathering of these Triassic plutons illustrates how deep geochemical weathering shapes island landscapes over geological time.

properties.name: Trinil Paleontology Locality
properties.description: Historic fossil site along the Solo River where Eugène Dubois discovered the first Pithecanthropus erectus ('Java Man') fossils in 1891.
properties.discovery_locality: Solo River banks at Trinil, Ngawi
properties.evidence_description: Original Pithecanthropus erectus (Homo erectus) skullcap (calotte) and femur recovered from Middle Pleistocene Solo River terrace gravels.
properties.evidence_significance: Fossilized skullcap and limb bones provide empirical evidence supporting bipedal Pleistocene hominin presence along ancient Javanese river valleys.
properties.why_it_matters: Trinil is the historic site of Eugène Dubois's 1891 discovery of 'Java Man' (Homo erectus), pivotal in establishing paleoanthropology as a rigorous scientific discipline.
properties.source: Dubois (1894) / Museum Geologi Bandung Reference Catalog

properties.name: Ciletuh Geopark Metamorphic Complex
properties.description: The oldest exposed rock formation in West Java, showcasing Cretaceous subduction melange (sheared tectonic mixture), ophiolites (ancient oceanic crust), and ultra-high-pressure metamorphic schist.
properties.evidence_description: Accretionary subduction melange containing sheared serpentinized peridotite, gabbro, ophiolite fragments, and high-pressure quartz-mica schist.
properties.evidence_significance: Tectonic melange and metamorphic schist provide physical evidence consistent with ocean floor accretion and deep subduction trench thrusting.
properties.why_it_matters: Ciletuh exposes West Java's oldest rock basement, containing Cretaceous ophiolites and metamorphic schists uplifted from an ancient subduction trench, preserving evidence of early Indonesian arc-trench convergence.

properties.name: Mount Rinjani & Segara Anak Caldera
properties.description: A active stratovolcano complex on Lombok featuring the 6 x 8.5 km Segara Anak caldera created by the catastrophic 1257 CE Samalas eruption.
properties.evidence_description: The 6 x 8.5 km Segara Anak caldera depression and extensive pumice tuff beds deposited during the 1257 CE Samalas volcanic collapse.
properties.evidence_significance: Caldera geometry and pumice blankets support the interpretation of major paroxysmal caldera-forming eruptions during historic times.
properties.why_it_matters: The 1257 Samalas (Rinjani) eruption was one of the largest explosive volcanic events of the last millennium, depositing widespread pumice across Lombok and driving a major global sulfur aerosol cooling event.
properties.source: Lavigne et al. (2013) PNAS / Smithsonian GVP (#264040)

properties.name: Maros-Pangkep Tower Karst Complex
properties.description: Spectacular tower karst landscape formed by Eocene-Miocene limestone uplift, underground drainage dissolution, and steep cliff erosion.
properties.evidence_description: Tower-shaped limestone karst cliffs and cave systems dissolved into Eocene-Miocene Tonasa Limestone formations.
properties.evidence_significance: Vertical cliff towers and solution caves provide physical evidence of extensive carbonate uplift followed by tropical meteoric dissolution.
properties.why_it_matters: Maros-Pangkep is one of the world's most spectacular tower karst landscapes, featuring tower-shaped limestone hills and ancient caves containing some of humanity's oldest documented rock art (~45,500 BP).
properties.source: UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List (#5981) / Aubert et al. (2014) Nature

properties.name: Mount Bromo & Tengger Caldera
properties.description: A active volcanic cone situated inside the 10 km wide Tengger Sand Sea caldera in East Java.
properties.evidence_description: Active volcanic cinder cones situated inside the 10 km wide Tengger Sand Sea caldera basin, surrounded by fine ash deposits.
properties.evidence_significance: Nested caldera basin structure provides evidence for multi-stage eruptive collapse followed by post-caldera cone building.
properties.why_it_matters: The Tengger Caldera complex showcases nested caldera collapse within a vast Sand Sea, demonstrating continuous post-caldera cone building and active ash venting.

properties.name: Great Sumatran Fault at Ngarai Sianok
properties.description: A dramatic 100 m deep canyon cut into volcanic tuff along the active dextral strike-slip Great Sumatran Fault line near Bukittinggi.
properties.evidence_description: A 100 m deep vertical canyon carved into volcanic ash tuff along the dextral strike-slip Great Sumatran Fault zone.
properties.evidence_significance: Displaced terrace deposits and linear gorge geometry provide physical evidence consistent with active strike-slip fault offset and river incision.
properties.why_it_matters: Ngarai Sianok is a dramatic canyon cut into volcanic tuff along the active Great Sumatran strike-slip fault system, illustrating dextral fault motion and rapid fluvial incision.
properties.source: Sieh & Natawidjaja (2000) JGR / Geological Survey of Indonesia

properties.name: Flores Liang Bua Paleontology Cave
properties.description: Limestone karst cave on Flores where the type specimen LB1 of Homo floresiensis ('the Hobbit') was discovered in 2003.
properties.fossil_material: LB1 partial skeleton, cranial elements, Stegodon florensis insularis fossils
properties.paleoenvironment: Subtropical karst cave deposit & woodland valley
properties.evidence_description: Type specimen LB1 partial skeleton and cranial remains of Homo floresiensis found in stratified cave sedimentary layers.
properties.evidence_significance: Endemic hominid skeletal fossils provide direct evidence supporting insular evolutionary dwarfing on Late Pleistocene oceanic islands.
properties.why_it_matters: Liang Bua is the type locality of Homo floresiensis ('the Hobbit'), revealing unique island dwarfing in hominins and expanding our understanding of Late Pleistocene human diversity.
properties.source: Brown et al. (2004) Nature / Sutikna et al. (2016) Nature

properties.name: Banda Arc & Weber Deep Basin
properties.description: Earth's deepest non-trench oceanic depression (~7.2 km deep), formed by detachment faulting behind the 180-degree curving Banda subduction arc.
properties.evidence_description: A ~7.2 km deep oceanic depression bound by low-angle extensional detachment faults behind the Banda subduction arc.
properties.evidence_significance: Bathyal detachment fault scarps and seabed topography support the interpretation of severe lithospheric extension in subduction back-arcs.
properties.why_it_matters: The Weber Deep is Earth's deepest non-trench oceanic basin (~7.2 km deep), formed by extreme detachment faulting behind the 180-degree curving Banda Arc subduction zone.
properties.source: Pownall et al. (2016) Geology / Geoscience Australia

properties.name: Bali Coastal Karst & Volcanic Terranes
properties.description: Illustrative candidate site demonstrating geological terrain features and data validation for educational entries.
properties.evidence_description: Illustrative coastal karst platforms and volcanic ash terraces used as an educational dataset reference.
properties.evidence_significance: Illustrative educational record demonstrating how coastal karst landforms are represented in geological mapping.
properties.why_it_matters: Illustrative educational record demonstrating how carbonate reef uplift and volcanic ash deposition interact to form coastal terranes.
properties.source: Illustrative educational example, not official data
